summary: Shoun Hino is a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under Keshav Pandurang Jog. He held a professorship at Gifu Pharmaceutical University (attested 2003).

Shozen Kumoi specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Otani University (~1938–1941) and under Erich Frauwallner (~1957–1959). He served at Otani University (assistant professor 1948–1981; emeritus ~1986–2017) and Bukkyo University (professor 1982).
Shri Krishna Saksena worked in philosophy and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Active in Indology and linguistics, Shri Krishna Sharma founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. He served as Assistant to the Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (1884), Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College, and permanent Professor of Sanskrit at Wilson College, Mumbai.
Working in the field of Indology, Shridhar Tryambak Pathak held posts as a Shastri at Deccan College (attested 1921) and as a Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar works in Indology and Buddhist studies, having studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He was Director at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (1981–2009) and Dalai Lama Chair Professor at Somaiya Vidyavihar University (attested 2024–2025).

Shrinarayan Mishra was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher who studied under Anantalal Thakur. His career at Banaras Hindu University included roles as Lecturer (attested 1971), Reader (attested 1985), and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 1987, 2010).

Shrinivasa Varakhedi works in Indology, philosophy, and computational fields. He served as Vice-chancellor of Kavikulaguru Kalidas Sanskrit University (attested 2019) and became Vice-chancellor of Central Sanskrit University (attested 2022).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar specialized in Indology and philosophy, studying under Kashinath Bapu Pathak and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He was Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1914–1937) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI (1948–1961).

Shrivatsa Goswami works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, having studied philosophy at Banaras Hindu University. He founded Sri Caitanya Prema Samsthana in 1972, taught at Banaras Hindu University, and was a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Shu-chen Chen works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under Jeffrey Hopkins, Karen Christina Lang, Bradley W. Reed, and Ronald G. Dimberg, and served as a teaching assistant there in 1996.

Shu-fen Chen is a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at National Tsing Hua University under Hans Henrich Hock and Chin-Fa Lien. She later became a professor at National Tsing Hua University (attested 2010).

Shubha Pathak specializes in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy, earning a PhD from the University of Chicago in 2007. She was a Senior Professor of Cultural Studies at FLAME University (attested 2023).

Shubhachandra is an Indology scholar who served as a professor at Karnatak University (attested 2001) and worked in the Department of Jainology and Prakrits at the University of Mysore (attested 2002).
Shubhangni Gupta works in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology as a doctoral student and PhD candidate at Stanford University (attested 2019, 2026).

Shuddhatam Prakash Jain works in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, holding degrees from multiple Indian universities. He taught at Central Sanskrit University (2003–2006), Mangalayatan University (2010–2013), and Ghanaram Hariram College (2014–2015).

Shudo Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Shigeo Kamata. He spent his career at Komazawa University, serving as assistant (1971), lecturer (1974), associate professor (1978), and professor (1984, 2014).

Shuhong Chang specialized in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology, studying in China and France. He held instructional posts at Zhejiang University and the Central Academy of Fine Arts before serving as director and honorary director of the Dunhuang Academy.

Shuichi Kato worked in Japanology, history, and philosophy, earning a medical doctorate at the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at the University of British Columbia (1960) and Sophia University (~1975–1985), and directed the Kyoto Museum for World Peace.
